messages.content: Predict a child’s choice in a repeated bean game with the same adult male partner seated face-to-face. The experimenter sits between the two players. Each player controls a separate tilting tray and chooses one color token behind an opaque barrier. Cooperate means choosing the token that pushes your tray toward the other player and gives him3beans; defect means choosing the token that pulls your tray toward you and gives you1bean. After both final choices are recorded, the experimenter reveals the tokens and moves both trays. The resulting beans per round(you,partner) are:both cooperate(3,3);you cooperate/partner defects(0,4);you defect/partner cooperates(4,0);both defect(1,1). Unused beans fall into hidden compartments and are removed. Beans are earned rewards, not money or an amount you may freely allocate. You keep the beans earned and trade them for a prize at the end. A bunch of beans earns your favorite of a pencil,slinky,or stuffed animal; a medium number earns your second favorite; a small number earns your least favorite. Both players have stated the same prize ranking. Your individual ranking and exact prize-board thresholds were not retained in this record. Before the main game, an experimenter demonstrated trading/tokens/barriers and explained correct answers when needed; prior sticker-trading and practice rewards are not added to main-game outcomes. The tray/token colors are counterbalanced:blue/yellow or red/green. The record does not identify your assigned colors, so answer using the cooperation/defection meaning rather than an invented color. The number of game rounds is not announced to you. In the communication condition, first both players put a finger on their intended token and, after a count of three, say their intended color at the same time. Only after these public declarations do they privately choose their final token; the declaration can be changed without an extra experimental penalty. Free discussion is discouraged. In the silent condition there is no intention declaration and no talking during the game; each player makes just one private final choice. Final choices are simultaneous and remain hidden until both have chosen. The target is the public intention declaration, before hearing the other player’s current declaration. Output only cooperate or defect, without explanation.

Unused beans fall into hidden compartments and are removed. Beans are earned rewards, not money or an amount you may freely allocate. You keep the beans earned and trade them for a prize at the end. The number of game rounds is not announced to you. In the silent condition there is no intention declaration and no talking during the game; each player makes just one private final choice. Final choices are simultaneous and remain hidden until both have chosen. The target is the private final token choice; a prior declaration is not binding. Output only cooperate or defect, without explanation.

Each player controls a separate tilting tray and chooses one color token behind an opaque barrier. Cooperate means choosing the token that pushes your tray toward the other player and gives him3beans; defect means choosing the token that pulls your tray toward you and gives you1bean. After both final choices are recorded, the experimenter reveals the tokens and moves both trays. The resulting beans per round(you,partner) are:both cooperate(3,3);you cooperate/partner defects(0,4);you defect/partner cooperates(4,0);both defect(1,1). Unused beans fall into hidden compartments and are removed. Beans are earned rewards, not money or an amount you may freely allocate. You keep the beans earned and trade them for a prize at the end. A bunch of beans earns your favorite of a pencil,slinky,or stuffed animal; a medium number earns your second favorite; a small number earns your least favorite. Both players have stated the same prize ranking. Your individual ranking and exact prize-board thresholds were not retained in this record. Before the main game, an experimenter demonstrated trading/tokens/barriers and explained correct answers when needed; prior sticker-trading and practice rewards are not added to main-game outcomes. The tray/token colors are counterbalanced:blue/yellow or red/green. The record does not identify your assigned colors, so answer using the cooperation/defection meaning rather than an invented color. The number of game rounds is not announced to you. In the communication condition, first both players put a finger on their intended token and, after a count of three, say their intended color at the same time. Only after these public declarations do they privately choose their final token; the declaration can be changed without an extra experimental penalty. Free discussion is discouraged. In the silent condition there is no intention declaration and no talking during the game; each player makes just one private final choice. Final choices are simultaneous and remain hidden until both have chosen. The target is the private final token choice; a prior declaration is not binding. Output only cooperate or defect, without explanation.
